value.body: A B.A. major in Hindi or another Indian language — Bengali, Marathi, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu, Sanskrit and others. It covers the language's literature across periods, grammar, linguistics, and practical writing; many courses add papers in translation, journalism or functional writing for offices.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12 in any stream. Central and many other universities admit through CUET-UG, where a language test can be one of the subjects counted; state universities and colleges often admit on Class 12 marks. Some programmes expect the language to have been studied at school.

value.title: At a glance
items: Most of the work is reading, close analysis of texts, and writing in the language.
Graduate jobs cluster around translation, media, publishing, content and teaching.
Central government translator and Rajbhasha posts usually ask for a Master's in Hindi or English.
School teaching needs a B.Ed; college teaching usually needs an M.A. plus UGC-NET or a Ph.D.

value.title: Undergraduate students in Indian languages
value.note: Covers Hindi and all other Indian languages at UG level, not only the B.A. major. The rise in 2023-24 is large for one year. AISHE counts responding institutions only; coverage varies by year, so part of any change may reflect reporting rather than real enrolment.
